_readme: biome look-research judgments (tools/biome_research.py). score 1-5: 1=broken, 3=reads, 5=hero. Weakest sort to the agenda top.

fungus_mycelium.note: hero — tapering filaments read as grown

flora_sdf_tree.note: solid closed canopy on a brown trunk; measured 746ms/cell — cost-flagged, densest maps should prefer flora:lsystem

fd_alien_lumen.note: Bioluminescent cracked cap reads instantly; glowing magenta cell-pattern is the family signature. Cap slightly lumpy but characterful.

fd_fairy_ring.note: Six pale caps in a legible ring - the colony-in-a-circle reads exactly. Individual mushrooms simple but clean.

fd_parasol_tall.note: Wide flat spiral-topped cap on a tall stem - parasol silhouette clear. Minor specks at the cap-stem junction.

fd_button_dome.note: Low rounded dome with a concentric top - the button reads cleanly; the humblest of the family, correctly so.

fd_shelf_bracket.note: STRIPING FIXED: the cap-edge cyan rainbow was the shader MEMBRANE surface (thin-film iridescence: fresnel x a UV rainbow), NOT the iridescence uniform - which is why zeroing that did nothing. Cap + gills switched to PETAL surface -> clean matte stacked shelves, no rainbow.

sf_wind_lean.note: Stem leans hard at ~45deg, cap turned - the wind pose reads dramatically. Minor gill striping under the cap edge.

sf_gravity_droop.note: Wide heavy cap sags at the edges over a short stem - the droop reads. Cap large but that is the pose.

sf_inflate_bloat.note: Swollen bulbous balloon cap over a short stem - the bloat reads convincingly.

sf_squash_settle.note: POSE FIX: wide flat LEVEL pancake cap on a squashed stem (was chunky+wild-tilt). Reads as pressed/settled now; level tilt is the key cue, moderate flatten keeps the gill striping off the top.

sf_wilt_collapse.note: STRIPING FIXED: same membrane->petal surface fix on cap + gills. The under-cap gill fan is matte now, no cyan banding. Reads as a clean wilted cap.

grub_a.note: Yellow-green SDF grub - continuous body, bulbous head, tail and small leg nubs, no joint holes. Reads as a larva. Cell-seeded individual A.

grub_b.note: Cyan SDF grub - same continuous body with a clearer side leg nub. Different cell, different colour and proportion. Individual B.

grub_c.note: Green SDF grub - consistent with the family: head, tail, leg nub, one watertight skin. Individual C. The trio reads as one species, three draws.

halo_flora.note: Green strip with grass blades and salmon blooms thinning outward - flora spills off the rim clearly.

halo_fungus.note: Pink mushroom cones and lavender caps scattered on the rim - reads as fungus thinning into the dark.

halo_fauna.note: CONTRAST FIX: warmer/lighter earth mounds + grey pebbles + a pale emissive egg (creature-sign) -> the rim reads as 'a creature nested here', not a dark-brown smear.

halo_mineral.note: Pale blue crystal shards scattered on the rim - reads as stone/mineral spilling out.

halo_water.note: Green reeds and flat lily pads at the rim - reads as a watery shore edge.

halo_meta.note: RULED CLOSED (correct by design, not a defect): scattered points of light are exactly what the not-alive kingdom should spill past the rim. It scores 3 because it is minimal, not because it is wrong — do NOT 'fix' it by adding matter. The other five halos carry cover; meta carries light.

fungus_ca_tuned.note: Teal voxel cubes - reads as the computed CA network frozen at a set rule/gen. Small but clearly a voxel structure, visibly computed.

meta_glyph.note: Cyan ring-and-cross rune hovering over its presence glow - reads clearly as the not-alive glyph, a rune of light.

flower_bluebell.note: Small blue bell bloom - reads as the tier-1 species. Tiny (right for t=1); the species colour/form differentiates cleanly.

flower_orchid.note: Pink blooms up a thin stem - reads as the tier-3 orchid species, distinct from bluebell/daisy. Small but legible.

flower_daisy.note: Yellow-centred bloom with petals and leaves - reads as the tier-5 daisy. The three-species ladder differentiates well by colour.

fungus_sdf.note: SIZE FIX: scale ~4x (was a chip next to fungus:dna's x4.6 boost) -> now a proper mushroom, cap flowing into stem as one continuous SDF surface.

mineral_crystal.note: CLUSTER FIX: 6-9 shards, x1.4 size, wider spread (was 4-6 tight 0.09-wide shards that merged) -> reads as a faceted crystal cluster of distinct prisms.

flora_tree.note: CANOPY FIX: bare twig -> fresh-green foliage mass on a short trunk. Sphere-blob leaves for lod<=2 (flat quads vanished at biome scale), leaves sized to the tree not the tip radius, leaf primary_color set to a living green. Reads as a leafy tree.

tree_a.note: Canopy fix - cell-seeded individual reads as a small leafy tree (blob canopy, visible trunk).

tree_b.note: Canopy fix - consistent leafy read across individuals.

tree_c.note: Canopy fix - best-developed of the trio, full blob canopy.
